headline: Bangor Water District easement for 10-inch water main at Harlow and Nelson streets is recommended to full council.
summary: The 20-foot-wide easement covers about 70 feet of city land at map 23, lot 162, on the corner of Nelson and Harlow. The water district would bore under the Kenduskeag Stream to build the main, and staff recommends approval. The committee also approved a $6,973.80 sewer abatement for 92 Sydney Street after a toilet leak was found. Director of engineering Jefferson Davis also gave an overview of the city's sewer and stormwater work.
decisions: Approved the $6,973.80 sewer abatement for 92 Sydney Street, 5-0.
Recommended the water district easement to the full council, 5-0.
discussion: Water main boring under stream: The water district would bore under the Kenduskeag Stream to link Harlow and Nelson streets. Boring under streams and highways was described as common, and the city recently bored under I-95.
Abatement cost questions: Questions were raised about whether the abatement covers the city's cost to treat the water. Answers were to be sent by email.
EPA sewer consent decree: The city has been under the decree since the 1990s and files yearly reports. Staff said the decree shapes much of the sewer budget and will not go away.
Kmart pump station capacity: Staff said rerouted sewer flow freed up 9,000 gallons a day of capacity for developments that had been waiting.

decision_evidence.quote: I I move a staff recommendation for the abatement. Second. ... Five yes, zero no.
I move staff recommendation to the full council. ... Five yes, zero no.

decision_titles: Water district easement at Harlow and Nelson streets
